metadata.title: Pass 3 reference table — AER-FGF8 mitogenic outgrowth coupled to the Sheth et al. (2012) fan-shaped autopod Turing solver
metadata.purpose: Parameters, source anchors and expected qualitative behaviours for the kinematic growing-domain (deforming Lagrangian mesh) extension added in Pass 3 of Slot 015. Closes the Pass 2 remediation item 'Couple the 2D polar fan-shaped limb bud Turing solver to a deforming tissue-mechanics mesh driven by localized AER-FGF8 mitogenic outgrowth'.
metadata.honesty_note: The Pass 3 coupling is a kinematic (prescribed-dilation) growth model: the area dilation rate g(r,t) is set directly by the AER-FGF8 mitogen field and the radial tissue velocity follows from mass conservation. No elastic constitutive law, stress balance or anisotropic cell-shape mechanics is solved; that residual is carried as an open Pass 4 remediation item.

sources.citation: Sheth R, Marcon L, Bastida MF, Junco M, Quintana L, Dahn R, Kmita M, Sharpe J, Ros MA (2012). Hox genes regulate digit patterning by controlling the wavelength of a Turing-type mechanism. Science 338(6113):1476-1480.
sources.used_for: Digit number N = L_autopod / lambda(H): digit period shrinks with distal Hox/Gli3 dose while autopod width sets how many wavelengths fit (Figs. 2-3).

sources.citation: Crampin EJ, Gaffney EA, Maini PK (1999). Reaction and diffusion on growing domains: scenarios for robust pattern formation. Bulletin of Mathematical Biology 61(6):1093-1120.
sources.used_for: Reaction-diffusion on a growing domain in Eulerian/ALE form: u_t + v . grad(u) + (div v) u = D Lap(u) + f(u,v); dilution term (div v) u; patterns on growing domains lag the fixed-domain wavelength until a mode transition (frequency doubling / peak insertion).

sources.citation: Boehm B, Westerberg H, Lesnicar-Pucko G, Raja S, Rautschka M, Cotterell J, Swoger J, Sharpe J (2010). The role of spatially controlled cell proliferation in limb bud morphogenesis. PLoS Biology 8(7):e1000420.
sources.used_for: Quantitative 3D limb bud proliferation maps: distally biased (AER-proximate) proliferation exists but is insufficient alone to explain limb bud shape; motivates the exponentially decaying FGF8 mitogen field M(r) = exp(-(R - r)/l_F) and the carried residual that oriented cell behaviours / mechanics are missing.

sources.citation: Summerbell D (1974). A quantitative analysis of the effect of excision of the AER from the chick limb-bud. Journal of Embryology and Experimental Morphology 32(3):651-660.
sources.used_for: AER excision arrests distal outgrowth; the earlier the excision the more proximal the truncation and the fewer distal skeletal elements form. Used as the qualitative anchor for the AER-ablation series (t_abl in {0.6, 1.2, 1.8} model time).

sources.citation: Kondo S, Miura T (2010). Reaction-diffusion model as a framework for understanding biological pattern formation. Science 329(5999):1616-1620.
sources.used_for: Review context: Turing pattern wavelength is set by kinetics/diffusion while the number of repeated elements scales with domain size (digit number = width / wavelength).

growth_model.mitogen_field: M(r, t) = A(t) * exp(-(R(t) - r) / l_F)   (AER-FGF8 secreted at the distal rim r = R(t), decaying proximally with length l_F)
growth_model.area_dilation_rate: g(r, t) = g_max * M(r, t)   (prescribed kinematic growth; div v = g)
growth_model.radial_tissue_velocity: v(r, t) = (1 / r) * integral_{r_prox}^{r} g(r', t) r' dr'   (mass conservation in the polar sector; purely radial flow so the sector angle Theta is fixed and the arc Theta * r widens)
growth_model.aer_activity: A(t) = 1 for t <= t_aer_off; A(t) = exp(-(t - t_aer_off) / tau_aer) afterwards (AER regression); A(t) = 0 for t >= t_abl in the ablation series
growth_model.reaction_diffusion_ale_form: u_t|_rho = -(v - w) u_r - g u + D_u Lap(u) + f_u u + f_v v - u^3 ;  v_t|_rho = -(v - w) v_r - g v + D_v Lap(v) + g_u u + g_v v, with mesh velocity w = rho * dR/dt on the computational coordinate rho = (r - r_prox)/(R - r_prox) in [0, 1]
growth_model.radial_anisotropy: D_r = eps_r * D for both species (eps_r = 0.05); stripe (digit-ray) orientation is therefore imposed by PD/AP diffusion anisotropy standing in for the Fgf/Wnt proximodistal modulation of Raspopovic et al. (2014) — carried as an open item
growth_model.gene_expression_noise: additive seeded Gaussian forcing of amplitude 0.02 * sqrt(dt) per step so that newly generated distal tissue carries pattern-seeding fluctuations

parameters.theta_span_note: 0.55 * pi (same sector angle as the Pass 2 fixed-width fan)
parameters.R_target_note: 2 / 0.55: the distal arc Theta * R_target = 2 * pi nondimensional = 2500 um (Sheth et al. 2012 constant autopod width)
parameters.g_max_calibration: g_max is solved (Brent root find on the outgrowth ODE alone) so that the WT distal arc reaches 2500 um at T_total; g_max = 1.95 for the default parameters

expected_behaviours.digit_number_width_law: N_digits increases monotonically with final autopod arc L(T) at fixed Hox dose and with k_c(H) at fixed width (Sheth et al. 2012; Kondo & Miura 2010); formalized as Lean 4 Theorem 4 sheth_growing_autopod_digit_number_law
expected_behaviours.growth_dilution_threshold: the modal eigenvalue on a growing domain is sigma_g(k) = sigma(k) - g; patterning proceeds during outgrowth only if sigma_max > g_rim (Crampin et al. 1999); formalized as Lean 4 Theorem 5 sheth_growth_dilution_turing_threshold
expected_behaviours.growth_induced_wavelength_lag: patterns laid down while the arc is short are stretched by subsequent outgrowth and persist while they remain inside the Turing band, so N_grow <= L(T)/lambda(H) with the deficit largest for the widest band (WT); Crampin et al. (1999) peak-insertion scenario
expected_behaviours.aer_ablation: earlier AER ablation -> smaller L(T) -> fewer digit wavelengths (Summerbell 1974 qualitative truncation ordering)
